tasks.short: Design, introduce and check a programme for storing, protecting, retrieving and retaining business records.

steps.what: Inventory record types, repositories, owners and existing access controls.
Agree record classes, retention needs, access responsibilities and retrieval requirements.
Draft the filing scheme, retention schedule and records handling procedures.

loop.input: Agreed records requirements, existing policy and approved procedure template.
loop.output: Draft procedures with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check every retention rule against approved requirements; reject invented periods and unsupported legal claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per section; unresolved conflicts return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure, but local handling instructions require rewriting source prose.

steps.what: Approve retention rules, access responsibilities and the programme rollout.
Configure filing locations, metadata, permissions and retention controls.
Explain new filing responsibilities and practise retrieval with departmental representatives.
Sample records and check filing, access, retention and retrieval compliance.
Authorize corrections and resolve disputed retention, access or disposal exceptions.

tasks.design: Configure classification, access and retention controls in the {DOCS}, with a records register in the {WORKFLOW} where existing metadata is insufficient. Read-only connectors on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assemble inventory and compliance evidence; a bounded drafting loop prepares procedures from agreed requirements. The records owner approves policy, control deployment and disputed disposal actions, while a {BI} dashboard shows exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repository metadata and ownership were inconsistent. Software could enforce rules, but people still had to settle retention duties and cross-department responsibilities.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing repository controls cover much of the execution. AI-assisted coding makes small connectors and checks cheaper to build; bounded drafting reduces procedure preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy migrations, legal holds, poor metadata and conflicting retention duties remain costly. GDPR applies; employee consultation and works-council requirements depend on national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve competing business, privacy and evidential needs, and secure agreement on who is accountable for records.

ambition.what: Records readiness review for new internal projects

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time assembling inventories and more time resolving ownership gaps and testing retrieval. Within an agreed remit, they can require records requirements before a project launches; retention and disposal authority stays with the records owner.

reach.task: Resolve misfiled records and missing metadata.
reach.learn: Learn practical classification problems and how staff search for records.

reach.task: Set departmental records responsibilities during organisational changes.
reach.learn: Learn service ownership, escalation paths and rollout planning.

evidence.claim: Repository configuration can enforce metadata, access and retention rules once those rules are agreed.
Cross-repository inventory and compliance checks usually need connectors, mappings and human exception review.
GDPR applies to personal records; employee consultation requirements depend on national rules and the proposed controls.

assumptions: The first release covers selected repositories and record classes, rather than a complete historical migration.
A records owner can obtain legal advice and approve retention requirements.
Repository metadata can be read through supported interfaces or controlled exports.
Inventory checks use metadata where possible, limiting access to record contents.
unknowns: Which repositories, retention features and export interfaces are available?
Who can approve access changes, legal holds and disposal?
How complete are record ownership and classification metadata?
Which national rules, employee consultation duties and collective agreements apply?
Does the proposed processing require a GDPR impact assessment?
research_questions: Which record classes generate the most retrieval failures or retention disputes?
Can existing repository features replace a separate records register?
What evidence is needed to demonstrate that a record was retained, held or disposed of correctly?
new_work: Review inventory gaps and compliance exceptions.
Maintain repository connectors and record-class mappings.
Check drafted procedures against approved requirements.
Test retrieval and access controls after organisational changes.
Review proposed disposal actions and maintain legal holds.

tasks.short: Evaluate business forms and reports, design revisions, test them with users and approve controlled changes.

steps.what: Collect current forms, reports, change requests and completed examples.
Clarify the business purpose, user difficulties and decisions the artefact must support.
Map fields and calculations to source data, recipients and downstream dependencies.
Choose necessary fields, definitions, calculations and proposed changes.
Create revised layouts, instructions, validation rules and sample outputs.

loop.input: Field specification, approved templates, source instructions and wording requirements.
loop.output: Proposed labels and instructions inserted into deterministically generated layouts.
loop.check: Validate schema, required fields and calculations deterministically; check prose against source instructions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per artefact; unsupported wording goes to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Layout and validation are deterministic; changed instructions sometimes require rewriting free text. Skip the loop when approved wording exists.

steps.what: Observe users completing realistic cases and review report interpretations.
Approve the revised artefact and its effective date.
Publish the approved version, retire old copies and notify affected users.

tasks.design: Use the {WORKFLOW} to collect change requests and retrieve approved versions from the {DOCS}; connectors read declared dependencies from the {ERP} and {BI}. A deterministic generator builds layouts and validation tests, with a small drafting loop only for changed instructions. User testing and process-owner approval precede versioned publication through the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Form purpose and field definitions were often implicit. Manual version control and uncertain downstream dependencies made even small changes slow.
tasks.enabler_now: Schema-driven generation, existing approval features and inexpensive connector development reduce preparation work. A bounded loop can rewrite instructions without deciding which data the business needs.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden spreadsheet dependencies, conflicting metric definitions and inaccessible legacy formats remain difficult. Staff must test whether users understand the result.
tasks.human_edge: Decide which information earns its place, notice misleading reports and resolve disagreements about business meaning.

ambition.what: Pre-release form and report checks for small internal teams

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time testing comprehension and challenging unnecessary data collection. They can clear low-impact template changes within a delegated remit; process owners retain approval of business definitions and material changes.

reach.task: Help occasional users complete internal request forms.
reach.learn: Learn common misunderstandings, accessibility needs and reasons requests are returned.

reach.task: Assess the impact of changing fields and report calculations.
reach.learn: Learn schema contracts, dependency tracing and regression checks.

evidence.claim: Structured specifications support deterministic form generation, validation and versioned publication.
A documented report failure involved non-existent AI-generated sources, supporting explicit source checks for drafted content.
User comprehension and tacit downstream dependencies require observation and stakeholder review.

assumptions: The pilot covers a small family of internal forms or reports.
Current versions and approved templates can be identified.
The dependency register starts with known links and is checked by affected users.
Test cases use synthetic or appropriately protected examples.
unknowns: Which forms are documents, system screens or generated reports?
Who has authority to approve each type of change?
Which downstream calculations and unofficial copies depend on existing fields?
Are versioning, approval and publication features already available?
Do changed forms collect employee data or trigger consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which fields cause the most rework without supporting a clear decision?
Can existing forms be retired or merged before rebuilding them?
Which comprehension and accessibility tests should become release checks?
new_work: Maintain field definitions, templates and dependency mappings.
Review drafted wording and investigate unsupported instructions.
Recruit representative users for short tests.
Check that publication retires obsolete versions.
Update validation cases when business definitions change.

tasks.short: Assess storage needs, compare equipment and propose a workable layout and purchase recommendation.

steps.what: Survey the available space, current equipment, access routes and storage practices.
Calculate required capacity, growth allowance and equipment dimensions.
Request equipment specifications, prices and delivery information from suitable suppliers.
Compare equipment capacity, dimensions, total cost and delivery constraints.

loop.input: Supplier quotes and specification documents in varying formats.
loop.output: Source-linked dimensions, capacities, price components, delivery terms and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate units and required fields; calculate totals deterministically; verify critical dimensions against source documents.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per quote; missing or conflicting values return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Varied supplier documents need text extraction. Use direct field mapping instead when structured catalogues are available.

steps.what: Draw alternative equipment layouts in space-planning software.
Walk through options with users and select a practical layout.
Prepare the equipment recommendation, cost summary and installation requirements.
Approve the proposed equipment, layout and expenditure.

tasks.design: A parameterised generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} calculates capacity, compares costs and creates layout options for the {OTHER} space-planning software. Configure quote requests in the {PROCUREMENT}, with a bounded extraction loop for unstructured supplier documents, and generate the recommendation in the {DOCS}. Site measurement, practical layout selection and expenditure approval stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measurements, catalogue dimensions and local constraints were scattered across drawings and quotes. These infrequent projects rarely justified a custom planning tool.
tasks.enabler_now: Small calculation and drawing generators are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding. Existing geometry methods can check explicit constraints without needing an autonomous planner.
tasks.still_hard: Measurements, floor loads, escape routes, accessibility and installation feasibility need competent verification. A useful drawing cannot establish site safety or structural suitability.
tasks.human_edge: Notice awkward access, unsafe handling, overlooked building constraints and how staff actually use storage.

ambition.what: Compare reuse, consolidation and purchase before each storage investment

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time redrawing layouts and assembling quote tables, and more time observing use and testing alternatives. They gain no purchase or building-safety approval rights; the facilities manager and budget holder retain those decisions.

reach.task: Plan storage installation around building access and workplace use.
reach.learn: Learn site survey methods, installation sequencing and when specialist checks are needed.

reach.task: Arrange stock locations for practical retrieval and handling.
reach.learn: Learn movement patterns, peak demand and handling constraints that drawings can miss.

evidence.claim: Capacity calculations, quote comparisons and checks against explicit geometric constraints can use deterministic code.
Unstructured supplier documents can be extracted into a common comparison schema with source checks.
Physical suitability and workplace safety require site evidence and competent human review.

assumptions: Storage means physical shelving, cabinets or similar workplace equipment.
The pilot covers one site and a limited equipment catalogue.
A competent person supplies applicable clearances and load constraints.
The generator proposes layouts within supplied constraints; it does not certify compliance.
Build ranges cover the planning aid, not equipment delivery or installation.
unknowns: Are current site drawings accurate and dimensioned?
Which equipment types, floor loads and access restrictions apply?
Can existing space-planning software already generate suitable options?
Are supplier catalogues structured or supplied as documents?
Who must approve installation, safety and expenditure?
Does a workplace change require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Can retention changes or consolidation remove the need for new equipment?
Which layout checks can the existing space-planning software already perform?
How often does this task recur, and would configuration cost less than a reusable generator?
new_work: Maintain equipment dimensions, units and cost components.
Verify extracted quote fields and resolve missing specifications.
Update site constraints after building changes.
Check generated layouts against on-site measurements.
Retain specialist reviews and approval evidence with the recommendation.

role.altitude: The management analyst shifts from assembling documents and comparisons toward testing whether procedures work in practice. Delegated authority can cover routine template changes and project readiness checks; legal, expenditure and site-safety decisions remain with designated approvers.
reach: Help administrative services managers introduce records requirements before organisational changes.
Work with computer systems analysts to trace data dependencies and validate form changes.
Help facilities managers compare storage alternatives using verified site constraints.
skills_to_grow: Translate business requirements into testable rules and schemas.
Configure workflows, permissions and version controls.
Trace data lineage and assess change impact.
Evaluate bounded model outputs against approved sources.
Run user observations and practical site reviews.
Understand GDPR and applicable national consultation requirements.
role.ambitious_version: Offer an internal operational design service that checks records readiness, form usability and physical storage alternatives before teams commit money or introduce new procedures.
